original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Prove cost(M)=delta(M) for every invertible target at every role count over a central local K-algebra, in the base-field right-vector alphabet with arbitrary free GL_n(K) maps.
scope_change_reason: This is an algebraic side result extending the local case of #4265 and the two-role theorem of #4276. It changes the role-count boundary, rather than adding a priced physical connector operation. It is not a supplier improvement.
bottleneck_link: An exact formal-alphabet cost separates local-algebra reachability from nonlocal matrix-block obstructions at arbitrary role counts. Native coefficient preparation, frames, routing, restoration, precision and stock remain unknown; no completed supplier budget is claimed.
stop_rule: Stop at the first verified arbitrary-role local theorem or a precise obstruction. Do not extend the search after the first improvement; put product-algebra and physical-caller questions in Open next questions.
evidence: PROOF.md proves the arbitrary-field, arbitrary-role local theorem. The self-contained verifier checks 2380 distinct sampled targets over five local algebras at n=3,4,5, with 27616 basis-data executions, 2688 direct delta-chart evaluations and eight controls. These are finite corroboration, not a complete multiplication theorem. The original card's positive control passed with 945 pairings. Advance claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19131568.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: For invertible targets with n>=3 over a product of two local algebras, which simultaneous pivot flags characterize cost equal to delta?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This would locate the first obstruction to extending the arbitrary-role local theorem to products.
open_questions.first_step: Specify one three-role pair over F2 x F2 and compare its common-chart column construction with the column lower bound.
open_questions.blocked_by: The proof selects a scalar chart and unit pivot order in one local algebra; these choices may conflict across components.

open_questions.question: Can one literal native producer and consumer implement a column replacement with a favorable complete invoice?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The formal cost does not by itself supply a recursive saving.
open_questions.first_step: Specify one algebra-valued coefficient's preparation, access, frame conversion and restoration contract before implementing a caller.
open_questions.blocked_by: Coefficient preparation, routing, restoration, precision, stock and physical supplier costs are unknown.
